clue.text: Wander about town

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of wander are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone strolls aimlessly around a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges WANDER. DARWEN is a mill town in Lancashire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwen is a market town in Lancashire, so it is an example of a place of that kind.

clue.text: An old soldier is more artful!

explanation.surface: A veteran fighter is said to be cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman was a soldier of old armies; arch means cunning, so its comparative means slyer.

clue.text: A youngster found guilty of pinching?

explanation.surface: A child is convicted of stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child is called a little one in British slang; someone who nips is one who pinches or squeezes.

clue.text: Protection for big cats-none may be trapped

parts.note: big means great

indicators.note: may be trapped tells us the nil letter is caught inside the word cats

parts.note: none is nil, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A zoo plans shelter for lions and tigers, hoping none is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big cats' reads as one phrase meaning lions and tigers; 'may be trapped' is the container signal, and none as the letter O is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy overcoats shield the wearer from cold, so they are a form of protection.

clue.text: Consolation is also perhaps given by the church

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of also could be some other arrangement

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Comfort is offered by the clergy as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' gives SOLA, the anagram of the fodder; 'given by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean comfort given to someone in grief or distress.

clue.text: Relation possibly from the other side of the world

definitions.text: from the other side of the world

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of relation could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A family member may live far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RELATION; 'Relation' looks like the definition but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern, from Asia, which lies on the far side of the globe from Britain.

clue.text: This drink is put into a bag, note

indicators.note: put into says the word is goes inside the word for a bag

parts.note: a net is a mesh bag
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bottle of liqueur is packed in a carrier along with a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message, but it is the musical TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet liqueur flavoured with aniseed.

clue.text: Day's end-flat time

parts.note: flat means level or even
tide is an old word for time, as in Christmastide

explanation.surface: A calm, level evening closes the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, when daylight closes.

clue.text: Recovered and went through it all over again

definitions.text: went through it all over again

explanation.surface: Someone got better and then told the story again from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is retreaded or given a new top when re-covered; to recap is to summarise again.

clue.text: The minister has to have a meal around four

indicators.note: around says the word for eating goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: to dine is to have a meal
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The vicar must eat about four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four' looks like a time of day, but it is the Roman numeral IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is an old word for a clergyman or theologian.

clue.text: Components made by employees in steel-works

indicators.note: in places the word for workers inside the rearranged letters
works signals the letters of steel are worked into a new order

parts.note: employees are men, staff

explanation.surface: Parts produced by workers at a steelworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' gives ELETS, the anagram of the fodder; 'steel-works' looks like one place, a steel mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Elements are the basic parts or constituents of something.

clue.text: A six footer though not out of school

parts.note: a batsman not out in cricket is still in
a school of thought is a sect

explanation.surface: A tall person who still attends classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six footer' suggests a tall person, but it means a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Every insect has six legs, so it is a creature with six feet.

clue.text: Taking some path meandering about composes the spirit

indicators.note: meandering suggests the letters of some path wander into a new order

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Walking a winding trail calms the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meandering' rearranges SOME PATH into ATMOSPHE; RE (about) ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere is the mood or feeling of a place, its prevailing spirit.

clue.text: Entered into an agreement and cut down

explanation.surface: Someone signed a deal and then made reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to make a binding deal, and also to shrink or shorten.

clue.text: Competent soldiers at first turned back

indicators.note: at first puts the soldiers ahead of the word for skilled

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
versed means skilled or knowledgeable

explanation.surface: Skilled troops initially retreated.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversed means went backwards or was turned the opposite way.

clue.text: Smart sailor in getting under way

indicators.note: in says the word for a seaman sits inside the word for a sharp pain

parts.note: to smart is to sting
tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A clever seaman is setting off on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective meaning clever, but it is the verb to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting means beginning, setting off.

clue.text: Jumble? It's cheap rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish suggests the letters of it's cheap are rubbished into a new order

explanation.surface: A junk sale item is dismissed as tat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' rearranges ITS CHEAP; 'Jumble' looks like the anagram signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a medley or patchwork of borrowed pieces.

clue.text: Getting out more tonic maybe

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of tonic could be reordered

explanation.surface: A drinker asks for another tonic water.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraction is the act of drawing something out, as a tooth.

clue.text: A painter rising before others to make check

indicators.note: before puts the turned letters ahead of the word for the remainder
rising in a down clue reads the painter's letters upwards

parts.note: an RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: An artist gets up early to inspect things.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest is to stop or halt something's progress.

clue.text: The abuse of one caught in traffic

indicators.note: caught in says the numeral is trapped inside the word for commerce

parts.note: traffic means trade, dealing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Insults from a driver stuck in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' suggests a road jam, but it means trade, as in drug traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of abuse.

clue.text: The monster in charge will get progressively worse

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The monster in charge will get progressively worse': OGRESS sits in 'progressively', but 'charge will get' and 'worse' have no job in that reading, and no other parse is found; possibly misread
annotationWithheld.clue: The monster in charge will get progressively worse

clue.text: Blunders will reveal the defaulter in time

indicators.note: in places the word for a turncoat inside the word for an age

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is one who deserts or fails to keep faith

explanation.surface: Mistakes will expose a debtor eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed mistakes, especially in printing.

clue.text: Carol has got left inside for playing about

indicators.note: inside says the nautical word for left sits within the word for carol

parts.note: to carol is to sing
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A girl called Carol has gone in to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is the verb to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting means frolicking, larking around.

clue.text: Make some change in the current regulation

explanation.surface: A rule is altered in the present regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another; an electrical device turns the flow of current on or off.

clue.text: Music composed without a note being written

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the calm word goes round the other letters

parts.note: composed means calm, serene
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Music written with one note left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but means outside: SERENE goes round A and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a piece of music, especially one sung outside a lover's window.

clue.text: The Australian gardener?

explanation.surface: Is the man from down under a keen horticulturist?
explanation.definitionFit: Australian soldiers and men generally are nicknamed diggers; someone who digs the soil tends plants.

clue.text: May be down on a winger

definitions.text: May be down on a winger

parts.words: May be down on a winger
parts.note: down looks like being critical of a footballer, but it is soft plumage on a bird

explanation.surface: Someone might criticise a football wide player.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage, including the soft down, covers a bird's wings.
